To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we propose a new tree kernel for encoding syntactic parsing information, (b) we show that the kernel can be efficiently computed and (c) we demonstrate that the kernel is effective on the task of question classification and semantic role labeling

(i) the PT kernel outperforms all other kernels on both tasks; (ii) the PT kernel is the fastest kernel; (iii) the PT kernel performs better when the dependency tree is used as the syntactic input; (iv) the PT kernel does not work as well as the other kernels when the constituency tree is used as syntactic input.
the PT kernel improves over the state-of-the-art in the semantic role labeling and the question classification tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) What is the most effective kernel to be used with dependency and constituent syntactic trees for the task of semantic labeling and question classification? (2) How can the kernel be computed efficiently?
the following questions: (i) How can we efficiently compute tree kernels for parsing trees? (ii) What is the best parsing paradigm for a given task?
the following questions: How to efficiently compute a tree kernel? How to select the most relevant tree nodes? And, how to use a tree kernel in natural language learning tasks?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PT kernel, with a proper parsing paradigm, is the best choice for encoding syntactic parsing information for natural language learning.
the PT kernel is the best kernel for syntactic trees, in terms of both accuracy and computational cost, and that it can be applied to any syntactic tree.
, when using a dependency tree, the Partial Tree kernel is the best option.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PT kernel is an effective and efficient way for syntactic parsing information.
the PT kernel, which is the first to exploit the dependency trees in a non trivial way, is a promising tool for syntactic parsing in natural language processing.
the PT kernel is the best tree kernel for dependency trees.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PT kernel can be used in a wide range of natural language applications, where dependency parsing is more appropriate than the constituency one.
tree kernels can be efficiently applied to syntactic trees in order to improve the performance of machine learning methods.
the kernel running time can be significantly reduced while maintaining high performance.
